chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali ibn Matar, from some of our companions, who said:
I asked al-Rida عليه السلام about a man who cannot find water nor earth: may he perform tayammum with clay? He said: “Yes; it is clean earth and purifying water.”

Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: if he happens to be in a land covered by snow and has no way to reach earth, then let him break it and perform wudu with its water. But if he fears for himself because of that, he should place the inner side of his right palm upon the snow and move it over it with pressure, then lift it with whatever moisture of it is on it and wipe his face with it. Then he should place his left palm upon the snow and do with it as he did with the right, and wipe with it his right hand from the elbow to the fingertips lightly like oil. Then he should place his right hand upon the snow as he placed it the first time and wipe with it his left hand from its elbow to the fingertips. Then he should lift it and wipe with it the front of his head, and wipe his feet with the wetness of his hands from the snow, and let him pray, if Allah wills. If he needs purification by ghusl, he should use the snow as he used it in his wudu, by pressing and wiping his head, face, and hands lightly like oil until he covers all of himself. But if he fears for himself because of that, he should delay the prayer until he is able to attain purification with water, or until he loses it and finds earth so that he may use it, and make up what he missed, if Allah the Exalted wills.

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: ritual dry ablution performed in place of wudu or ghusl under certain conditions
key_terms.الثَّلْجِ: snow, discussed here as a substitute source for purification when earth is inaccessible
key_terms.الطِّينِ: clay, used here in the context of whether tayammum may be done with it
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: ritual bath required for major purification
key_terms.صَعِيدٌ: earthly ground or surface material suitable for tayammum
key_terms.طَهُورٌ: purifying, describing water that can be used for ritual purification
key_terms.وُضُوئِهِ: his wudu, meaning the ritual ablution for prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do for wudu or tayammum if only snow or clay is available?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses rulings of ritual purification when water and earth are unavailable or difficult to use, especially in conditions of snow. It explains the permissibility of tayammum with clay, the use of melted snow for wudu, and an alternative wiping method with snow when direct use of water may be harmful.
